messages:
Jordan K: FYI customer ClearLogix just pinged — their wire for INV-2024-789 ($124,500) was returned by their bank. They got a short return note: "Beneficiary bank not found / invalid SWIFT/BIC". Can finance/ops advise next steps? Customer needs this cleared urgently, they have PO CLX-PO-556.

PaymentsBot: Payment update: wire_id=WD-983211 returned status=RCV_REJECTED code=SWIFT_NOT_FOUND timestamp=2024-06-03T13:02:18Z. Trace=TRC-7721.

Ella F: Thanks Jordan. Can you paste the original wire instructions (redact acct#)? We need: receiving bank name, SWIFT/BIC, account name, account number/IBAN, and any intermediary bank. Also need remittance proof from customer showing date/time they initiated. Without that we can't file a recall.

Jordan K: Pasting redacted snippet from their wire request: 
```
Beneficiary: ClearLogix Ltd.
Acct/IBAN: ****-XXXX-1234
Bank: BalticBank PLC
BIC/SWIFT: BBALXXXXXXX
Intermediary: (none provided)
Amount: 124500.00 USD
Reference: INV-2024-789 / CLX-PO-556
```
Customer says their bank used ABA routing instead of IBAN when initiating — they attach a screenshot that says "Routing number/recipient mismatch".

Ryan O: If the originating bank picked ABA for an international transfer, that's likely the mismatch. Two quick items: 1) Confirm whether this was sent as domestic ACH vs SWIFT wire — PaymentsBot trace shows SWIFT return. 2) Don't reissue funds until finance confirms recall status. We should ask customer to get their bank to confirm the exact SWIFT/BIC they used and provide a SWIFT MT103 or payment confirmation.

Michael S: Customer-facing ask we can send them (short): 
```
Hi ClearLogix — please ask your bank for the MT103 / payment confirmation showing the sending BIC/ABA used and the trace number. Also confirm the exact account number format they sent (IBAN vs domestic account). If possible, ask them to reinitiate using the receiving bank's IBAN + BIC and include our invoice ref.
Thanks — Redwood Support
```

Ella F: Once we have MT103 and the sending bank trace we can open a recall with our bank. If returned for "Beneficiary bank not found" the money should be returned to originator, but timing varies (3-10 business days). For urgent cases we can request an expedited investigation but need the docs. Also note: since this is cross-border, intermediary bank routing can cause failures — ask the customer to include intermediary BIC next time.

Jordan K: Customer replied: their bank claims they used beneficiary BIC "BBALXXXXXXX" but got auto-reject "No route to beneficiary bank". They want us to confirm beneficiary bank details so they can re-wire.

Ryan O: Confirmed — Redwood side: beneficiary bank recorded is BalticBank PLC, BIC BBALXXXXXXX (we pulled from our billing portal). Two checks for customer: 1) Make sure there are no extra leading zeros/spaces in account/IBAN. 2) For USD wires to BalticBank they may need an intermediary bank (e.g., USNBRXXXX) — if their bank doesn't automatically route, they should ask their bank to include the intermediary.

PaymentsBot: Note: previous successful wires to ClearLogix used intermediary USNBRXXXX. No other returns in last 12 months.

Ella F: Action items for us: Jordan please get (A) redacted MT103 or payment confirmation from customer, (B) copy of bank return message, (C) confirmation of whether their bank initiated via SWIFT or used domestic rails. Finance will not reissue or apply credits until we either get funds back or get a signed PO/instruction authorizing us to resend.

Michael S: Also flagging: if customer asks us to re-issue without proof of returned funds, we need signed PO + indemnity. Avoid sending net new invoice credit until bank completes recall.

Jordan K: Sent above checklist to customer and asked for MT103. They replied with a short PDF (redacted) that includes: MT103 trace=TRX-4490, sender BIC=SNDGUS33, message says "Payment returned: Beneficiary unknown". They say their bank will open an investigation but estimated 5-7 business days.

Ella F: Ok — we'll open a recall with our bank using the trace. FYI ops: if funds are returned, do we have a standard flow to mark invoice as unpaid and re-open billing? I can create a journal entry once funds are returned.

Ryan O: Yes — ops: mark invoice as returned, generate credit note once funds are received back, then accept new payment. I can draft the ops runbook for returned wires (steps: intake docs -> open bank recall -> monitor trace -> mark invoice -> create credit note).

PaymentBot: Investigation opened with bank reference BKINV-2109. Next update scheduled in 48 hours.

Ella F: One more heads-up — because PO CLX-PO-556 references a net-30, customer may request we hold service while they sort payments. For billing side: if they need access maintained, we can temporarily allow a limited grace after approval from rev ops. Jordan keep me posted if they ask.

Jordan K: Will do. I'll chase MT103 updates and intermediary BIC confirmation. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Michael S: Thanks — looping back when bank returns or we get MT103 update. :white_check_mark:
